memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife; that would dishonour your brother. Do not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. Do not have sexual relations with either her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter; they are her close relatives. That is wickedness. Do not take your wife's sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while your wife is living.'" - Lev 18:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the last verse especially. Do not take your wife's sister as a rival wife. The word rival tells you exactly what God is preventing.

Jacob's household is the case study. He married Leah and Rachel, sisters, and their home became a battleground of jealousy and competition that scarred both women and shaped their sons for the worse. Scripture tells that story without approving of it — and here God legislates so it does not happen again.

Notice what God is protecting: a woman's dignity within her own marriage. She should not have to compete for her husband with her own sister. She should not live in a household organised around rivalry.

The Bible describes polygamy in its narratives; it does not commend it. Every polygamous household in Scripture is troubled. And Jesus took marriage back to the beginning — the two will become one flesh. So they are no longer two, but one flesh (Matt 19:5-6). Two. Not two and a rival.

God's design has always been for a marriage where a spouse is secure, not competing. Where love is not divided.

If you are married, that is worth examining. Is there anything in your marriage that makes your spouse feel they are competing? Work, screens, another relationship, your family of origin?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does anything in your home make your spouse feel they are competing?
2. How does Jesus' return to "the two shall become one" shape your view of marriage?
3. What would help the people closest to you feel secure this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You protect the dignity of those who could be pushed aside. In my closest relationships, make me faithful, undivided and safe to be near. Amen.
